jobs.employer_name: Weierstraß-Institut für Angewandte Analysis und Stochastik (WIAS)
jobs.description: The Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics (WIAS) is an institute of the Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V. (FVB). The FVB comprises seven non-university research institutes in Berlin which are funded by the federal and state governments. The research institutes belong to the Leibniz Association.WIAS invites applications for aResearch Assistant Position (f/m/d)(Ref. 26/22)in the Research Group “Nonsmooth Variational Problems and Operator Equations”(Head: Prof. Dr. Michael Hintermüller),starting on January 1, 2027.Field of work:The successful candidate will work in the MATH+ project "DOC-TWIN: Duality-Based Error Control for Optimal Control Problems in Digital-Twin-Based Structural Health Monitoring". The project aims at developing a convex-duality-based framework for reliable error control in PDE-constrained optimal control problems motivated by digital-twin-based structural health monitoring.The Tasks include:- Developing and analyzing duality-based a posteriori error identities for PDE-constrained optimal control problems;- Deriving corresponding discrete a priori error identities and using them for convergence-rate analysis and certified nonlinear solver control;- Designing, implementing, and numerically validating finite element methods, including adaptive mesh-refinement strategies and suitable post-processing techniques;- Preparing scientific publications and presenting the results at workshops and conferences.**We are looking for: **Applicants with:- A very good university degree in mathematics, computational science, engineering, or a closely related field;- A strong interest in numerical analysis, optimization, partial differential equations, or scientific computing;- A willingness to work on both the mathematical analysis and the implementation of numerical methods for PDE-constrained optimization problems;- Good communication skills and the ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment;- Good written and spoken English skills.Desirable Qualifications:Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage but not a requirement:- Finite element methods, adaptive methods, or a posteriori error estimation;- Convex analysis, nonsmooth optimization, or optimal control;- PDE-constrained optimization or inverse problems;- Numerical methods for elasticity, structural mechanics, or related models;- Implementation of numerical methods in Python, MATLAB, Julia, C/C++, or finite element software.What we offer:- The opportunity to work at WIAS Berlin, a leading research institution with strengths in partial differential equations, mathematical modeling, nonlinear optimization, and applied mathematics in general;- The option of mobile working;- A certified family-friendly work environment (Audit berufundfamilie);- The opportunity to live and work in Berlin, one of the world's most culturally rich and diverse international cities. Berlin offers a wide range of opportunities to enjoy life outside work while remaining relatively affordable compared with other major cities. Neither the position nor living in Berlin requires knowledge of German, although WIAS offers free German courses. We particularly welcome international applicants. Berlin also offers a rich scientific landscape, with numerous research opportunities and career prospects in both academia and industry;- Close mentorship from the supervisor and other peers through a dedicated mentorship program.Please direct scientific queries to Prof Dr. Michael Hintermüller (michael.hintermueller@wias-berlin.de).The appointment is limited to two years. The position is full-time (39 hours per week), with a salary based on pay grade E 13 of the German TVöD Bund pay scale.WIAS is committed to fostering diversity and equal opportunities and particularly encourages women to apply. Applicants with disabilities will be given preferential consideration in cases of equal qualification. If you have any questions or want to provide us with information related to diversity, inclusion or disabilities, please feel free to consult our website orcontact our Diversity Officer, Sara Krummenacher (sara.krummenacher@wias-berlin.de).How to apply:Please upload your complete application documents (motivation letter, detailed CV, certificates, copy of the master thesis, etc.) via our applicant portal using the button “Apply online”.The application period opens immediately and remains open until the position is filled.We are looking forward to your application!

jobs.occupation: Lead Engineer - Applied AI & Data Products (Leiter/in - Engineering)

environments, taking full technical ownership.• Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Guide and develop engineers within your team, shape our applied AI engineering practices, and ensure project and team success.• Thought Leadership: Represent SQUER's applied AI expertise externally — through client relationships, internal knowledge-sharing, or community engagement.Your qualifications• Extensive Software Engineering Experience: Several years of hands-on and architectural experience in software engineering (e.g., Python, Java, C#, JS/TS, or similar).• Applied AI Depth: Proven, independent experience applying AI services in production (e.g., LLMs, NLP APIs, cognitive services), not just experimenting.• Cloud Platform Ownership: Confident designing and deploying AI-driven features on AWS, GCP, or Azure at production scale.• Data & API Architecture: Strong understanding of data processing, APIs, and databases (SQL & NoSQL), with the ability to make architectural decisions independently.• Leadership & Mentorship: Ability to guide, coach, and develop other engineers, and to take responsibility for a team's delivery and satisfaction.• Customer-Facing Confidence: Comfortable representing SQUER independently to customers with a high degree of professionalism.• Languages: Fluency in German and English.Your Benefits Why You'll Love Working at SQUER:• Ownership & Responsibility : at SQUER, we believe in empowering our team. In our flat hierarchies, your ideas and actions matter more than titles. Take the reins, make an impact and grow with us.• Learn & Grow : Tap into a € 5.000 annual training budget to sharpen your skills and take advantage of our in-house Leadership Academy. Join and be part of our active tech community through meetups, hackathons and training sessions. Get up to 40h/year additional time off for your personal education.• Exciting Challenges & Real Impact : Dive into diverse projects where your work truly makes a difference – for our clients and for SQUER.• Flexibility for Performance : Benefit from hybrid work options, flexible hours, workations within the EU, and additional vacation days – giving you the freedom to perform at your best.• Tailored Tools for Success : Choose your preferred hardware configuration and leverage our suite of AI tools and licenses (Anthropic, OpenAI, and more) to suit your working style.• We Value You : Beyond perks and benefits, we offer a competitive annual salary to recognize your exceptional contributions.• Be Part of a Thriving Team Culture : At SQUER, collaboration and connection are at the heart of what we do. Purpose of your JobOur Science and Technology team is looking for a Modelling Scientist to advance data-driven drug development through cutting-edge computational approaches.In this role, you will apply mechanistic models, machine learning, and molecular simulations to predict the stability and behaviour of biopharmaceutical products. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to integrate modelling into experimental workflows and support innovative, model-informed development strategies.Are you passionate about scientific modelling and pharmaceutical innovation?Join us and shape the future of computational drug development—apply today!Your Responsibility- Act as a scientific contributor in cross-functional research and development projects, supporting the integration of advanced modelling approaches into biopharmaceutical development.- Develop, validate, and apply advanced computational models to simulate the physical and chemicals stability, as well as the behaviour, of biopharmaceutical drug products.- Integrate experimental and structural data into predictive modelling frameworks.- Utilize a range of modelling techniques, including mechanistic models, machine learning approaches, and molecular simulations, to generate actionable scientific insights.- Contribute to the development of internal modelling platforms, tools, and workflows to enhance scalability and reproducibility.- Design and execute simulation studies to investigate formulations parameters, degradation pathways, and process related risks.- Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams including formulation scientists, analytical experts, and business developers to align modelling strategies with project objectives.- Analyse and interpret complex data to generate actionable insights.- Translate and present complex modelling outcomes into clear, impactful recommendations for internal stakeholders and project teams.- Ensure model quality through rigorous validation procedures and documentation, following internal standards and regulatory expectations where applicable.- Drive continuous innovation by exploring and implementing state-of-the-art computational approaches relevant to pharmaceutical formulation science.- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of developments in computational modelling, data science, and biopharmaceutical development to ensure the scientific relevance and competitiveness of modelling approaches.- Contribute to scientific excellence by co-authoring peer-reviewed publications.- Support regulatory submissions by providing modelling data and documentation as needed.What you need to succeed- Master’s degree or higher in Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field (PhD preferred)- Formal training or academic coursework in mechanistic modelling, machine learning, bioinformatics, or molecular dynamics is advantageous.- 2–5 years of experience in pharmaceutical research and computational modelling, ideally with exposure to protein- and nucleic acid-based therapeutics.- Strong programming and data analysis skills, with proficiency in tools such as Python, MATLAB, or R, and familiarity with modelling and simulation libraries.- Expertise in mechanistic modelling, machine learning, molecular modelling, or molecular dynamics simulations.- Solid understanding of biopharmaceutical products, including structure-function relationships, degradation mechanisms, and formulation challenges.- Experience in integrating computational models into experimental workflows and interdisciplinary project settings.- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving capabilities, with a track record of scientific contributions such as peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations.- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex modelling results into clear insights for diverse audiences.- Fluency in English, both written and spoken.- Collaborative and team-oriented mindset with a proactive and open approach to interdisciplinary work.- A passion for scientific innovation, curiosity, and a commitment to staying at the forefront of computational and pharmaceutical science.Ergänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Grundkenntnisse: Modellbildung, Simulation (IT)Erweiterte Engineering, Quantitative Forschungsmethode, Laborarbeiten, Labortechnik, Programmiersprache R, Bioinformatik, Angewandte Mathematik, Biomathematik, Datenvisualisierung, Data Science, Machine LearningZwingend erforderlich: Forschung, Arzneimittelentwicklung, Pharmazeutische Technologie, Programmiersprache Python, Analysis
